messages:
anna: Heads-up — seeing intermittent OOMs from continuous-batcher when KV cache grows under heavy long-chat load. Profiling snapshot attached (gpu mem free dips ~200MB then OOM). Anyone else? :eyes:

matt: saw one earlier at 11:12 on canary. pattern looked like 2-3 long seqs (2k tokens) piled into single batch and killed kv allocation.

anna: exact. Profiling suggests per-request KV footprint ~= tokens * layers * kv_entry_size; rough estimate we use ~1.1KB/token for our 70B fp16 model. So two 2k requests ~4.4MB * layers? (math simplified) leads to unexpected growth when batch contains many long histories.

kevin: idea: add a preflight "kv_budget_check" during batch formation. maintain rolling sum of estimated_kv_bytes for candidate batch; if sum + incoming_estimate > max_kv_budget -> either stall or move request to next batch. Keep max_kv_budget = free_gpu_mem - reserved - headroom_factor.

sophia: agree but careful: moving requests can increase tail latency for short requests stuck behind long ones. propose token-budget targeting: keep two queues: short-path (kv_est < T) and regular. short-path gets immediate fast-path batching up to small batch_size; regular uses kv-aware formation.

anna: also want to avoid perf regressions from additional branching. we can implement a very cheap estimate func: cached_tokens = min(history_len, kv_cache_cap) * per_token_estimate. No mem allocs.

matt: kernel selection interplay: batching by token budget will create heterogenous seq lengths, which can force fallback kernels. Suggest we bucket by seq_len and kv_cost and only merge within same bucket if possible. bucket key = floor(log2(seq_len)) + kv_bucket.

kevin: posted a quick config snippet we can try on canary:

```
batcher:
  max_kv_budget_bytes: 800000000   # 800MB per GPU
  kv_safety_factor: 0.85
  short_path_threshold_tokens: 64
  bucket_binning: [0, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048]
  kv_est_per_token_bytes: 1100
  preflight_mode: reject_or_requeue  # options: stall, reject, requeue
```

sophia: +1 to requeue; stall risks thundering herd. Also add metrics: kv_budget_utilization, batch_requeues, short_path_tail_latency.

anna: next steps: kevin to implement preflight check + requeue, matt to add bucket-aware kernel selection hooks, sophia to add dashboards. Can we target a canary tomorrow? :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy queued: branch=kv-batcher-preflight, env=canary, owner=kevin

kevin: will push a PR this afternoon. I'll add perf experiment flags so we can A/B and watch for regressions.

sophia: also add unit test for pathological case: 3x 2k sequences arriving simultaneously should not OOM (should requeue to multiple batches). I'll own the test.

matt: great. capture in perf run: latency_p50/p95, OOM_count, kernel_fallback_rate.

anna: thanks team — let's keep it incremental and watch canary closely. :rocket:
